expl.summary: Every jet is placed on 16 scales, each a clipped sum of if-statements on jet observables; neuron 2 is constant and carries no information. Each class score adds some scales and subtracts others, and the largest score decides the class; the formula's validation accuracy is 79.3%. The g score relies mostly on the particle-multiplicity scale (neuron 1, +37%), on which gluons sit far highest (8.13), and on the low-mass scale (neuron 9, +18%), and subtracts the two-prong scale (neuron 4, -20%). The q score adds the low-mass scale (neuron 9, +29%) and subtracts the two-prong scale (neuron 4, -35%) and the multiplicity scale (neuron 1, -16%), so quarks and gluons are separated mainly by the number of particles. The W and Z scores both subtract the broad-jet scale (neuron 8, -24% and -26%), on which tops sit highest, and both add neuron 5 (pT held in the 50 hardest particles, mass above 56 GeV; +13% and +15%). W and Z are split by mass: neuron 0, which falls as the mass rises above 79 GeV, raises the W score (+11%) and lowers the Z score (-20%); neuron 7 (mass 92-100 GeV with pT kept within ΔR 0.3) raises the Z score (+10%) and lowers the W score (-7%); and neuron 14 (mass above 91 GeV) lowers the W score (-11%). The t score adds the angular-spread scale (neuron 10, +25%) and subtracts neuron 13 (pT within ΔR 0.3 at high total pT, -34%), on which tops sit lowest.

0.title: light jets: falls as the mass rises above 79 GeV
0.measures: Its two largest terms act on the jet mass with opposite signs: mass > 79.0 GeV pushes it down (share -0.273) and mass > 90.0 GeV pushes it up (+0.294), partly offsetting the first for the heaviest jets. Small mass/pT squared (< 0.0076) pushes it up (+0.111) and a mass of the 50 hardest particles above 82.0 GeV pushes it down (-0.101). Overall it falls with mass, mass/pT squared, λ₁+λ₂ and ΣzΔR² (rank correlations -0.735, -0.72, -0.72, -0.72). W jets sit highest (2.13), then quarks (1.30), gluons (0.67), Z (0.46) and tops (0.13); it is zero for 84.6% of tops, 40.8% of gluons, 16.0% of Z, 15.8% of quarks and 1.3% of W jets.
0.role: It lowers the Z score (-20%), where it is the second-largest input, and raises the W score (+11%) and, slightly, the t score (+2%); it does not enter the g or q scores. It separates W jets from the rest best (AUC 0.94).

1.title: many particles, pT spread beyond the hardest ones
1.measures: It follows the number of particles (rank correlation 0.748) and the number with pT > 1 GeV (0.729), and falls with the pT share of the 30 hardest particles (-0.708). Its strongest terms: a softest real particle below 2.3 GeV pushes it down (share -0.119; below 1.5 GeV it is pushed back up, +0.058), a pT share of the 50 hardest particles above 0.96 pushes it down (-0.105), log of total pT above 6.9 pushes it up (+0.084) and below 7.1 down (-0.086), and a pT of the 2 hardest particles below 710 GeV pushes it up (+0.083). Gluons sit far highest (8.13), then tops (3.84), quarks (2.36), Z (1.44) and W (1.28); it is zero for 46.8% of W, 39.9% of Z, 32.8% of quarks, 4.9% of tops and 1.2% of gluons. Its values reach 15.2, the widest range of the 16 neurons.
1.role: It raises the g score (+37%, its largest input) and lowers the q score (-16%), so it separates gluons from quarks by particle multiplicity; it does not enter the W, Z or t scores. Freezing it costs 7.6 points of accuracy, by far the most of any neuron.

2.title: constant, independent of the jet
2.measures: It has no if-statements: it equals 0.125 for every jet, so it carries no information about the jet.
2.role: It does not enter any class score in a way that depends on the jet: its tiny weight shares (+0.4% in the q score, -0.7% in the Z score) only shift those scores by a constant.

3.title: few particles, little radiation beyond ΔR 0.2
3.measures: Its strongest term is a particle count below 47 (share +0.29). It is also pushed up for fewer than 6 particles at 0.2 ≤ ΔR < 0.4 combined with a pT share of the 50 hardest particles above 0.97 (+0.163), for narrow jets whose first of 3 subjets is light (ΣzΔR² < 0.009 and subjet mass < 30.0 GeV, +0.128), for a harder of 2 subjets lighter than 27.0 GeV (+0.108) and for fewer than 9.4 particles at 0.1 ≤ ΔR < 0.2 (+0.086); small τ₂₁ (< 0.34) pushes it down (-0.134). It falls with the number of particles, τ₄ and τ₃ (rank correlations -0.832, -0.811, -0.794). Quarks sit highest (1.34), then W (1.13) and Z (0.84); gluons (0.28) and tops (0.10) are low, and it is zero for 74.9% of tops and 49.4% of gluons.
3.role: It lowers the g score (-9%) and raises the W score (+5%) and the Z score (+5%); it does not enter the q or t scores.

4.measures: Its largest term is linear in the pT of the 30 hardest particles and pushes it down (share -0.342).
